65: ### BR-006 replacement — Database-managed catalog
66: 
67: `identifier_schemes` is a database-managed global reference catalog. Party Registry runtime MUST read it but MUST NOT mutate it. Catalog creation or change is allowed only through the governed database-management path. Runtime database credentials SHOULD be least-privileged so application execution cannot `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, or `DELETE` rows in `identifier_schemes`.
68: 
69: ### BR-022 replacement impact — Runtime lifecycle
70: 
71: The Party and Party Identifier transition matrices remain unchanged. Identifier Scheme status values remain persisted catalog metadata, but Party Registry V1 exposes no runtime operation that transitions them. Any database-level change of scheme status is governed outside the Party Registry application API.
72: 
73: ### BR-023 replacement impact — Scheme mutability
74: 
75: Identifier Scheme mutability is not an application concern in V1. Party Registry runtime treats all scheme fields as read-only. Database-governed changes must preserve the DBML constraints and compatibility with deployed normalizer/validator implementations.
76: 
77: ### BR-027 replacement — Runtime rule compatibility
78: 
79: Party Registry owns the versioned application-code catalog of supported normalizer and validator implementations. The database-managed Identifier Scheme catalog stores only implementation keys, never executable code. During identifier processing and readiness checks, the runtime MUST reject/fail closed when required persisted scheme configuration references an unsupported or unavailable implementation. Adding a new implementation still requires a software release; adding or changing a scheme row requires the governed database-management path rather than a runtime Scheme Administration use case.
80: 
81: ### FR-019 replacement — No Scheme creation use case
82: 
83: Party Registry V1 MUST NOT expose a runtime Identifier Scheme creation operation. Scheme records are provisioned through governed database management.
84: 
85: ### FR-040 through FR-045 replacement — No Scheme API surface
86: 
87: Party Registry V1 MUST NOT expose Identifier Scheme lookup, search, update, status-transition, retire, delete, or administration operations as application use cases or REST resources. Runtime scheme access is internal read-only reference access used by Party Identifier processing.
88: 
89: ### FR-048 replacement impact — Rule-catalog validation
90: 
91: WHEN Party Identifier processing references a database-managed Identifier Scheme, THE SYSTEM MUST verify that its normalizer/validator keys are supported by the running software before accepting the identifier. No Scheme create/update/activation API is implied.
92: 
93: ### FR-049 unchanged — Readiness
94: 
95: Persisted scheme configuration that requires an unavailable implementation continues to make readiness unavailable and dependent identifier operations fail without business-state mutation.
96: 
97: ### IR-004 replacement impact
98: 
99: Database-managed Identifier Scheme catalog changes are not tenant Party integration events and MUST NOT create Party Registry outbox events.
100: 
101: ## 5. Acceptance criteria replacements
102: 
103: ### AC-006 replacement
104: 
105: GIVEN the Party Registry V1 API and application use-case surface, WHEN operations are enumerated, THEN no Identifier Scheme create/update/status/delete operation exists and runtime code has no business use case capable of mutating the catalog.
106: 
107: ### AC-051 replacement
108: 
109: GIVEN a new Identifier Scheme such as a supported document type is required, WHEN it is introduced, THEN the change occurs through a reviewed database-management artifact/process rather than a Party Registry REST command.
110: 
111: ### AC-052 through AC-056 replacement
112: 
113: GIVEN Party Registry runtime is operating, WHEN Identifier Scheme access occurs, THEN it is internal read-only access required by Party Identifier processing. No runtime lookup/search administration resource, update, transition, retire, or delete operation is exposed.
114: 
115: ### AC-057 replacement
116: 
117: GIVEN any database-managed Identifier Scheme catalog change, WHEN it is applied, THEN no tenant Party outbox event is generated for that catalog change.
118: 
119: ### AC-077 replacement
120: 
121: GIVEN a database-managed scheme references an implementation key unsupported by the running Party Registry version, WHEN identifier processing or readiness validation occurs, THEN the dependent operation fails without changing Party/Identifier/outbox state and readiness reflects the unusable required configuration where applicable.
122: 
123: ### AC-078 replacement
124: 
125: GIVEN a database migration/data-administration change introduces or changes an Identifier Scheme, WHEN the change is validated for release, THEN its implementation keys must exist in the deployed/released application catalog before that scheme is usable by Party Identifier processing.
126: 
127: ## 6. Database and privilege consequence
128: 
129: The DBML continues to contain `identifier_schemes`; no table/column deletion is authorized by this clarification.
130: 
131: The application runtime access model is:
132: 
133: ```text
134: identifier_schemes
135:     runtime SELECT: allowed
136:     runtime INSERT: forbidden
137:     runtime UPDATE: forbidden
138:     runtime DELETE: forbidden
139: ```
